sections.title: Medical history for dental care
sections.alert: Plan extractions and surgery around these risks, with the physician where needed. Warfarin: INR ideally within 24 hours (72 hours if stable); delay if 4 or above. DOAC: no change for 1 to 3 simple extractions; miss or delay the morning dose for surgical or more extensive work. Antiplatelets: do not stop. Antiresorptive or anti-angiogenic drug, or head and neck radiotherapy: note the risk of jaw osteonecrosis. Prosthetic valve or previous endocarditis: follow the infective endocarditis protocol.

sections.title: Red flags: spreading infection
sections.alert: Possible Ludwig angina or spreading deep neck infection: send to the emergency department now for airway assessment and maxillofacial or ENT surgical care. Do not delay for dental treatment.

sections.alert: Possible oral cancer or dysplasia: refer urgently to oral and maxillofacial surgery or ENT for biopsy, and advise stopping tobacco and areca nut.

advice.title: Daily care of teeth and gums
advice.text: Brush your teeth twice a day for at least two minutes with a fluoride toothpaste. Cut down sweets, sugary snacks and fizzy drinks, especially between meals, and drink water instead. Have your mouth checked by a dentist regularly.

advice.title: Tobacco, areca nut and mouth cancer
advice.text: Stop all tobacco, smoked or chewed (bidi, cigarettes, gutka, khaini), and areca nut (supari, paan). Tobacco damages the gums, and tobacco and areca nut are leading causes of mouth cancer; ask us for help to quit. Look inside your mouth regularly, and see a dentist or doctor without delay if an ulcer or a white or red patch has not healed in 2 weeks. Do not put tobacco or anything else on it.

advice.title: Toothache and swelling
advice.text: Until your treatment, keep the area clean and rinse with warm salt water. Do not put tobacco, camphor, salt, balm or heat on the tooth or the swollen cheek, and take only the medicines prescribed for you. Go to the hospital emergency department at once if the swelling spreads, or you have fever or difficulty opening your mouth, swallowing or breathing.

advice.title: After a tooth extraction
advice.text: If the socket bleeds, place a rolled, damp gauze or clean cotton pad over it and bite firmly for 20 minutes. For the next 24 hours avoid smoking, alcohol and exercise, keep your head raised and do not disturb the clot. If bleeding continues after a second 20 minutes of pressure, come to the hospital straight away; if you take blood-thinning medicine, come as soon as bleeding fails to stop or starts again.
